survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is a governance overview of Sweden’s adult skills system and does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC). As a result, there is no assessment sampling frame, no plausible-value (PV) scaling, and no student-level survey weighting or replicate-weight design to apply. The tables describe institutional responsibilities and expenditure shares at subnational levels (regions and municipalities), not survey-based student achievement outcomes. If analysts were to extend this note with ILSA microdata, they would need to use the official ILSA sampling weights (and replicate weights where provided) from the relevant Data Explorer/IDB, but such weighting is not part of the present document.

Instead, it summarizes governance structures, stakeholder responsibilities, and expenditure shares across levels of government. Similarly, missing-data handling is not reported because there is no statistical estimation on microdata; the content is descriptive and policy-institutional.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Sweden country note provides a descriptive overview of how the adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels. It explains that national ministries set policy frameworks, while implementation is carried out by a mix of national agencies, deconcentrated local offices, social partners, and municipalities. The note distinguishes responsibilities across policy areas (VET/HVET, CET, AE, and ALMPs) and across governance levels, including the statutory role of Sweden’s 21 regions and the autonomy of 290 municipalities. It also highlights recent reforms, such as strengthened regional responsibilities and the introduction of a new upper-secondary vocational education for adults programme for targeted, industry-relevant training. Because the document is not an empirical ILSA-based analysis, it does not report ML model performance, benchmarks, or achievement metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to ILSA/ML fields because the document is a policy governance country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment study. There is no student sample, no assessment domain scoring, and no predictive modeling pipeline to extract. Consequently, fields such as PV handling, missing-data handling, ML techniques, and main findings are intentionally empty or not applicable by design.
